source_refs.note: Exercise 10.1, Question 23 (book p. 278); the book prints no answers for Exercise 10.1; answers checked with sympy and the solution book

blocks.explanation:
A difference of two cosines equals a sine; the angles \(2x\) and \(6x\) average to \(4x\), the angle on the right.
To find: the solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\) and the general solution.
Plan: use \(\cos C - \cos D\) to get \(\sin 4x\) as a factor, bring everything to one side, factorise and solve each factor.
steps:
Given: \(\cos 2x - \cos 6x = \sin 4x\).
To find: the solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\) and the general solution.
Method: \(\cos C - \cos D = -2\sin\frac{C+D}{2}\sin\frac{C-D}{2}\) with \(C = 2x\), \(D = 6x\).

Use the difference formula
\[\cos 2x - \cos 6x = -2\sin 4x\sin(-2x)\]
\[= 2\sin 4x\sin 2x\]
Why: \(\frac{C+D}{2} = 4x\), \(\frac{C-D}{2} = -2x\), and \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\).

Factorise
\[2\sin 4x\sin 2x - \sin 4x = 0\]
\[\sin 4x(2\sin 2x - 1) = 0\]
\[\sin 4x = 0 \text{ or } \sin 2x = \tfrac{1}{2}\]
Why: \(\sin 4x\) is common; never divide by it, or the roots of \(\sin 4x = 0\) are lost.

When \(\sin 4x = 0\)
\[4x = n\pi \;\Rightarrow\; x = \tfrac{n\pi}{4}\]
In \([0, 2\pi]\) (\(n = 0, \ldots, 8\)):
\[0, \tfrac{\pi}{4}, \tfrac{\pi}{2}, \tfrac{3\pi}{4}, \pi, \tfrac{5\pi}{4}, \tfrac{3\pi}{2}, \tfrac{7\pi}{4}, 2\pi\]
Why: sine is zero at every multiple of \(\pi\).

When \(\sin 2x = \frac{1}{2}\)
\[2x = \tfrac{\pi}{6} + 2n\pi \text{ or } \tfrac{5\pi}{6} + 2n\pi\]
\[x = \tfrac{\pi}{12} + n\pi \text{ or } \tfrac{5\pi}{12} + n\pi\]
In \([0, 2\pi]\): \(\frac{\pi}{12}, \frac{13\pi}{12}, \frac{5\pi}{12}, \frac{17\pi}{12}\).
Why: sine is positive in quadrants I and II, reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{6}\); divide by 2.

Collect the answers
\[\left\{\tfrac{n\pi}{4}\right\} \cup \left\{\tfrac{\pi}{12} + n\pi\right\} \cup \left\{\tfrac{5\pi}{12} + n\pi\right\}\]
Why: \(\frac{\pi}{12}\) and \(\frac{5\pi}{12}\) are not multiples of \(\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{3\pi}{12}\), so nothing is counted twice: \(9 + 4 = 13\) values in \([0, 2\pi]\).

Check: \(x = \frac{\pi}{12}\)
\[\cos\tfrac{\pi}{6} - \cos\tfrac{\pi}{2} = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - 0 = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
\[\sin\tfrac{\pi}{3} = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \;\checkmark\]
Why: both sides give the same number.
blocks.final_answer:
In \([0, 2\pi]\) (13 values): \(x = 0, \frac{\pi}{12}, \frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{5\pi}{12}, \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3\pi}{4}, \pi, \frac{13\pi}{12}, \frac{5\pi}{4}, \frac{17\pi}{12}, \frac{3\pi}{2}, \frac{7\pi}{4}, 2\pi\)
General solution \(= \left\{\frac{n\pi}{4}\right\} \cup \left\{\frac{\pi}{12} + n\pi\right\} \cup \left\{\frac{5\pi}{12} + n\pi\right\}\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\)
